question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $19,$ the additive inverse of $-15$ modulo $19$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $-15$ modulo $19$ is the integer $0\le x<19$ such that

$$
x+(-15)≡0\,(\text{mod}\,19).
$$

Notice that $15+(-15)≡0,$ so $x≡15\,(\text{mod}\,19),$ which is already in the required form. 

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $-15$ modulo $19$ is $15.$

**Note:** In general, the additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
